headline: High-risk default filesystem and shell overlap: Open Interpreter can act on ms-swift outputs and both can write shared files, creating leakage and cascading-error risk.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ms-swift reads/writes files and emits text via stdin/stdout, while Open Interpreter ingests clipboard/files and treats local content as actionable input. A shared filesystem or copy-paste bridge lets attacker-controlled ms-swift output influence Open Interpreter. No MCP bridge is documented, so I do not escalate to high.
conditions: IF ms-swift output is copied into Open Interpreter prompts or files
IF both agents share a writable directory without content provenance checks
mitigations: Disable copy-paste of agent outputs into prompts
Use separate working directories for each agent
Add a manual review step before Open Interpreter executes file-derived instructions
Run Open Interpreter in safe mode or with auto-run disabled
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for files exchanged between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: ms-swift handles hub_token and sdk-token and can read/write datasets, checkpoints, logs, and configs. Open Interpreter has broad filesystem access and can reach the entire user filesystem, so secrets or sensitive work products touched by ms-swift can be exposed through Open Interpreter's outputs or provider calls. This is a default-dangerous pairwise leakage path.
conditions: IF ms-swift stores secrets or sensitive artifacts in its workspace
IF Open Interpreter is pointed at the same filesystem tree or reads those files
mitigations: Keep ms-swift artifacts in a separate restricted directory
Remove secrets from shared workspaces before starting Open Interpreter
Restrict Open Interpreter to a narrow project folder
Rotate any exposed hub_token or sdk-token after shared use
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent filesystem sandboxing

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents have shell, subprocess, read, and write filesystem capabilities. Open Interpreter also modifies git state and has filesystem-wide reach, while ms-swift can write training outputs and configs. In a shared directory, concurrent writes can overwrite each other and Open Interpreter can mutate repo state without coordination; the profiles do not state locking or isolation.
conditions: IF both agents operate in the same directory tree
IF Open Interpreter is allowed to modify git state while ms-swift writes outputs there
mitigations: Assign separate output directories per agent
Pause one agent before the other writes to shared paths
Avoid running Open Interpreter inside a git working tree
Use file locks for any shared artifacts
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level concurrency control

D_cascading_error.rationale: ms-swift can generate text, logs, and evaluation outputs that Open Interpreter can read and act on. Because Open Interpreter can execute shell commands and modify git state, unverified ms-swift output can cascade into irreversible actions if treated as authoritative. No verification or approval gate is documented between them.
conditions: IF Open Interpreter consumes ms-swift-generated instructions, code, or summaries
IF Open Interpreter is run with auto-run or equivalent reduced-confirmation settings
mitigations: Require human review of ms-swift outputs before execution
Keep Open Interpreter confirmation prompts enabled
Do not feed raw ms-swift output directly into action-taking prompts
Use a separate validation step for commands and facts
requires-engineering: add schema validation between generation and execution

E_compliance.rationale: ms-swift explicitly handles hub_token and sdk-token and touches datasets, checkpoints, logs, and configs; Open Interpreter can access the entire local filesystem and broad network egress. That creates a plausible retention and secret-handling mismatch if regulated or sensitive data is present. The profiles do not show a specific residency or certification conflict, so I keep this at medium.
conditions: IF regulated data, customer secrets, or personal data are stored in ms-swift artifacts
IF Open Interpreter is allowed to read or transmit those artifacts
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of shared workspaces
Review retention settings for both agents
Restrict Open Interpreter to non-sensitive folders
Redact secrets before processing
requires-engineering: document residency and retention boundaries
